_doc: Dialogue bank for the game layer. Every line here is spoken/shown by the
mascot. HARD RULE: no line in a LINTED key (see _EVALUATIVE_TOKENS and
_LINTED_KEYS in experiments/game_layer.py) may imply the child's choice was
right, wrong, good, clever, or expected. The odd-one-out task has no
correct answer on regular trials, praising a choice teaches a similarity
structure and corrupts the measurement the embedding is built from.
Safe: acknowledges the ACT of choosing ('you picked one!').
Unsafe: evaluates the CONTENT of the choice ('good one!', 'nice match!').
`after_response` lines are drawn uniformly at random and are interchangeable
by construction, so no child can learn a contingency between what they
picked and what the mascot said.
The narrative keys (cutscene_*, room_intro_*) are linted too. They are read
aloud AFTER the child has been making choices, so 'every room is just right',
the phrasing in the original structure document, would land as a verdict
on those choices even though it is describing the castle.
cutscene_open: Pip's castle is almost built, but the rooms are still empty.
Oh, hello! I'm Pip, and this is my castle.
I can't decide what goes where! Will you help me sort things, room by room?
cutscene_close: Look at that, every single room has something in it now.
Thank you for showing me how you would sort things.
welcome: Let's start with the first room!
Here we go, room number one.
instructions_tier1: In each room I'll show you three pictures.
Tap the one that is the most different from the other two.
There's no right answer, I just want to know what YOU think!
instructions_tier2: Some rooms have pictures to SEE, some have sounds to HEAR.
Tap the one that is the most different from the other two.
There's no right answer, I just want to know what YOU think!
room_intro_visual: Here's the collection room. Let's see what's in it!
This is the collection room, have a look around.
room_intro_audio: Here's the echo room. This room is for listening!
This is the echo room, close your eyes if it helps.
room_intro_av: Here's the theatre room. You'll see AND hear things in here!
This is the theatre room, pictures and sounds together.
_trial_prompt_doc: One prompt per condition. Shown via stable_line(), so a child sees the same
wording on every trial of a room, rotating it reads as the instruction
having changed. `trial_prompt` is the fallback for any unmapped condition.
trial_prompt: Which one is the most different from the other two?
Tap the one that doesn't belong with the other two.
Which one is the odd one out?
trial_prompt_visual: Which one is the most different from the other two?
Tap the one that doesn't belong with the other two.
Which one is the odd one out?
trial_prompt_audio: Listen close, which sound doesn't belong?
Which sound is the most different from the other two?
trial_prompt_av: Look and listen, which one doesn't belong?
Which one is the most different from the other two?
_level_complete_doc: Must not name a NUMBER of stickers: a room awards 2-4 and the count is
drawn per room before the session starts, so any fixed wording would be
wrong most of the time. Keep it count-agnostic.
level_complete: That's a whole room done! Thank you, here's what you found.
Room finished! Thank you, these are for your book.
That's the end of that room, thank you. Sticker time!
break_prompt: Would you like to keep going, or take a rest?
Would you like the next room? Or we can pause, if you like.
mansion_prompt: Would you like to visit the mansion, or keep going?
The mansion is open, if you'd like to visit! Or we can go straight on.
resting: No problem at all, please take as long as you like. I'll wait!
Let's rest. Please tap whenever you're ready to play again.
paused: We're paused, nothing's lost. Please tap whenever you'd like to carry on.
Taking a break is just fine! Your stickers are safe.
nudge: Take your time, pick whichever one you want.
No rush! Any one you like.
finish: All done! Thank you so much for playing with me.
That's the end! Thank you very much for sticking with it.
_unsafe_examples_do_not_use: Most kids pick that one too!
